quote: One cannot think well, love well, sleep well, if one has not dined well.
source: Virginia Woolf, A Room of One’s Own, chapter 1 (1929)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg of Australia text, downloaded whole and searched; the sentence read in its paragraph, and the chapter divisions counted so that the paragraph falls between the headings ONE and TWO
evidence.edition: A Room of One’s Own, 1929 (Project Gutenberg of Australia eBook 0200791)
evidence.locator: chapter 1, in the Fernham dinner passage, after the sentence on heart, body and brain all mixed together

reason: Word for word, and in chapter 1: the paragraph sits well inside the first of the six numbered sections, in the account of the dinner at Fernham. It is Woolf’s own narrating voice, not a character, so no speaker is named. Caution for the editor, not a fault in the citation: the Mrs Dalloway carry in 01-fict-06 is already held for June, and one person can appear only once in a month.
